audit.whatIsWrong: Warwick's passive and W are swapped throughout. Five fields call the healing 'Blood Hunt passive', and the early text says 'His W (Eternal Hunger) fury stacks'. In fact Eternal Hunger is the passive (bonus magic damage on attacks that heals him below 50% health, tripled below 25%) and Blood Hunt is the W (move speed toward and attack speed against low-health targets, 80 s cooldown at rank 1). Blood Hunt heals nothing.
audit.why: The whole low-HP sustain plan hinges on knowing which bar to watch. Telling the reader to deny 'fury stacks' on a W that has no stacks sends them looking for a mechanic that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Eternal Hunger named as the passive healing source in whys[0], whys[4], early, mid, spikes[1] and wants.you[1]; Blood Hunt left as the W speed tool.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 is given to Swain at 8/10 while its own why says Warwick wins straight trades. Levels 4-5 and First item sit at 'Skill' though their whys describe the anti-heal window and the poke spike as yours, and 2+ items is Swain although the why concedes his flank threat. Packet chart: Skill/Swain/Swain/Swain/Swain/Swain/Skill.
audit.why: Four rows disagreed with their own explanations at a 53.81% win rate over 197 games.
audit.corrected: Row 0 to Skill (5/10), rows 3 and 5 to Swain (7/10), row 6 to Skill (5/10); win[] and phases[].side proposed as pairs.

audit.why: Four spikes present: Level 2 root, Level 6 Demonic Ascension, first item, and Warwick's Infinite Duress. Only the ultimate's cooldown was missing.
audit.corrected: Infinite Duress given its 1.5 s suppress and 110 s rank-1 cooldown so the post-ult window is countable.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Don't about fighting without anti-heal carries only filler text; nothing states that Jaws of the Beast damages a share of your maximum health.
audit.why: Riot's text: damage based on target maximum health, healing for damage dealt. That makes armour the wrong purchase and anti-heal the right one — the flagged missing interaction for this matchup.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d now states the max-health bite and that armour misreads it.

edits.before: Warwick's level-1 auto-attack pressure and Blood Hunt passive self-sustain win straight trades — stay at Q range, deny fury stacks, and do not hand him free autos.
edits.after: Warwick's level-1 auto pressure and Eternal Hunger (passive) healing win straight trades — that heal doubles under 50% HP and triples under 25%, so stay at Q range.

edits.before: Demonic Ascension outheals his Blood Hunt sustain in any extended fight; bait his Infinite Duress by dipping to medium HP, then activate R and drain him down through the suppress.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension outheals his Eternal Hunger sustain in any extended fight; bait Infinite Duress by dipping to medium HP, then activate R once the 1.5 s suppress is spent.

edits.before: Demonic Ascension turns every extended fight in your favor: Warwick's Blood Hunt healing cannot compete with drain + fragment sustain, and you keep R charges to deny his all-in window.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension turns every extended fight in your favor: Warwick's Eternal Hunger healing cannot compete with drain + fragment sustain, and R denies his all-in window.

edits.before: Infinite Duress suppresses you mid-R drain — keep your R active before he can land it, or flash the channel to deny the kill window entirely.
edits.after: Infinite Duress suppresses for 1.5 s and is down 110 s at rank 1 — once he spends it, the next stretch of lane belongs to you outright.

edits.before: Keep Demonic Ascension active in extended trades so his Blood Hunt passive healing is outpaced by your drain
edits.after: Keep Demonic Ascension active in extended trades so his Eternal Hunger passive healing is outpaced by your drain

edits.before: At level 1 Warwick has respectable auto-attack pressure and Blood Hunt passive that heals harder as you go low — do not trade autos with him freely, sit at Q range and last-hit. The moment you hit level 2 and have E, this lane flips: Warwick has no dash and no escape, so a clean E-root into passive-pull into Q burst punishes every time he steps forward. His W (Eternal Hunger) fury stacks require him to auto you to build — deny autos at all costs and you deny his setup. By level 3 your W-slow into E-root is a kill threat he cannot sidestep, and you should be piling up Soul Fragments every time he mispositions.
edits.after: At level 1 Warwick has respectable auto-attack pressure and Eternal Hunger, a passive that heals him harder as HE goes low — do not trade autos freely, sit at Q range and last-hit. The moment you hit level 2 and have E, this lane flips: Warwick has no dash and no escape, so a clean E-root into passive-pull into Q burst punishes every time he steps forward. His passive heals off every attack he lands, so denying autos denies his sustain outright. By level 3 your W-slow into E-root is a kill threat he cannot sidestep, and you should be piling up Soul Fragments every time he mispositions.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a slow grind where Warwick tries to brute-force short trades, banking on his Q (Jaws of the Beast) self-heal to sustain poke. Anti-heal (Bramble or Executioner's) is a priority purchase here — it cuts the Q heal roughly in half and turns every W-poke trade into a net HP loss for him. At level 6 the matchup is firmly yours: Demonic Ascension outheals Blood Hunt's scaling, and his only answer is Infinite Duress. Keep your R running before he can suppress you — a suppressed Swain with R already active continues draining through the CC, but if you activate R into the suppress you lose the cast. Bait his R by dipping to medium HP then drain him down.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a slow grind where Warwick brute-forces short trades, banking on Jaws of the Beast (Q) to bite a share of your max HP and heal him for it — armour does not answer that. Anti-heal (Bramble or Executioner's) is the priority purchase here: it turns every W-poke trade into a net HP loss for him. At level 6 the matchup is firmly yours — Demonic Ascension outheals his Eternal Hunger sustain, and his only answer is Infinite Duress, a 1.5 s suppress on a 110 s cooldown at rank 1. Bait it by dipping to medium HP, let him spend it, then run the full pattern while it is down.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: His Q bites a share of your max HP and heals him for it — armour misreads that.

notes: Warwick's passive and W were swapped across six fields — Eternal Hunger is the passive that heals; Blood Hunt is the W that grants move/attack speed against low-health targets and heals nothing. The old mid text claimed a Swain with R already active keeps draining through a suppress; that is not in Riot's text and I could not verify it, so the rewrite drops the claim rather than restating it. Chart rows 0, 3, 5 and 6 flipped to packet.levelChart as matched pairs.
